title: The Adelaida District
text: Chimney Rock Road and Nacimiento Lake Drive form part of the boundary of the Adelaida District, the wine district in the far western part of the Paso Robles region. The district climbs the Santa Lucia Range, from foothills at about 900 feet to high slopes at about 2,200 feet. Here the ocean's influence is modest, with light sea breezes and little fog. Its soils are thin, lying on bedrock, and much of it is calcareous, meaning rich in lime.

s1.quote: § 9.238 Adelaida District. ... Proceed easterly on San Miguel Road (locally known as Chimney Rock Road, then Nacimiento Lake Drive, then Godfrey Road, and then San Marcos Road) ... Proposed Adelaida District Region II-III transitional area with modest marine influence (light sea breezes and little marine fog) 25 30 Santa Lucia Range high mountain slopes grading to foothills; 900-2200 feet Shallow, bedrock residual soils and patchy colluvial hillside soils from middle member of Monterey Formation and older rocks; largely calcareous soils.
